description: Validates a boundary-scoped use-case model has been generated with complete actor/boundary/requirement traceability and linked detailed scripts

checks.description: A use-case model must exist for the target boundary
checks.remediation: Run usecase-generatemodel against the target boundary's domain/process/collaboration documents

checks.description: The model's boundary_ref must carry an explicit boundary_type, never left undeclared
checks.remediation: This skill must not generate a model against a boundary whose boundary_type is unknown or undeclared (contract Section 2.1) — stop and surface a clarification question instead

checks.description: Every use case must carry a primary_actor_ref and a boundary_ref matching the model's own boundary
checks.remediation: Ensure every use case references exactly one primary actor and the same boundary_id as its owning model

checks.description: Every use case must carry at least one requirement reference
checks.remediation: A use case with no supporting requirement should be reconsidered, not silently generated

checks.description: Every use case's script_ref must resolve to an existing script file with required sections
checks.remediation: Generate a linked script at use-case-scripts/UC-[###]-[slug].md for every modeled use case, with Trigger, Preconditions, Main Flow, and Postconditions sections at minimum

checks.description: Scripts for non-software or unknown-typed boundaries must never contain a UI References section
checks.remediation: UI References sections are only permitted when boundary_type is explicitly software AND a concrete Screen/UIModelEntry mapping exists for that step (contract Section 2.2)

checks.description: Use case IDs should follow the UC-[###] convention, scoped per boundary
checks.remediation: Use the UC-[###] zero-padded 3-digit format, scoped per boundary per contract Section 3.3 (not globally unique across the project)

checks.description: A changelog entry should be present documenting revision history, including any flagged unresolved references
checks.remediation: Document revision history; flag unresolved requirement/process references explicitly rather than silently dropping or renumbering existing use cases
